description_overview: Set aside WLD and USDC for someone you choose, while keeping access to your funds and earned income. Enter amounts, name an heir and choose a check-in interval; the app manages the asset contracts as one plan. New WLD and USDC balances use Morpho by default, after explicit fee and risk consent. Collect available income without withdrawing tracked principal or resetting the timer. Our service takes 10% only of realized positive net gains after strategy fees and loss recovery, never principal. Re7 also takes its separate strategy performance fee inside Morpho; the app displays the current rate before deposit. Returns vary, value can fall and cash withdrawals depend on liquidity. After a missed check-in, the heir must claim and wait seven days. You can renew until payment executes. Monitored eligible transfers are attempted automatically; the heir can also complete them manually. This smart-contract transfer plan is not a legal will.
description_how_it_works:
1. Sign in with World App wallet authentication. World ID verification is not required.
2. Enter WLD and USDC amounts, choose a contact, username or wallet address and set a check-in interval of 1–365 days. Review exact amounts, the full recipient address, service and strategy fees, and lending risks before opening the wallet. Missing asset contracts are created internally. WLD and USDC are never converted into each other. Existing balances remain accessible.
3. Approve your deposits in World App. If interrupted, resume the remaining setup; verified completed deposits are not sent again. Share your plan with the heir using World Chat or a link. Reminders require each recipient’s own permission.
4. Check in to all active assets from Home. Collect available income separately from principal withdrawals. Income collection does not reset the timer; an expired plan needs an explicit check-in first. Losses must be recovered before tracked capital becomes income.
5. After expiry the named heir files a claim and waits seven days. You can renew until transfer actually executes. The funded service attempts eligible monitored transfers; the heir can complete them in World App if the service is delayed or unavailable. Earlier basic vaults require manual completion.
6. Yield inheritance first attempts cash redemption. If unavailable, receipt shares and idle cash go to the fixed heir; the applicable positive-gain fee can be paid in shares. The heir can redeem wallet-held shares later as liquidity permits, without a second service fee.
7. WLD strategy rewards can be claimed and reinvested. USDC campaign WLD remains separate from USDC, with no silent conversion; its realized reward fee and USDC profit accounting are separate. Gifts are excluded from reward fees. Late canonical rewards remain owed to the original fixed recipient; keep the original contract link.

Strategy governance and fees can change. USDC can depeg or be frozen by its issuer. Campaign rewards and verified-human boosts are not guaranteed for this service. There is no fixed APY or principal guarantee. Network and service delays can affect timing.
description_connect: Our server verifies a one-use World App wallet signature and issues a one-hour wallet-bound session. User-approved token and factory transactions run on World Chain; we never collect private keys or seed phrases. Monitoring stores registered addresses, verified contract state, alert history and execution records. A dedicated signer pays gas only for eligible transfers to the contract’s fixed heir; it cannot file the claim, redirect funds or withdraw an active owner’s balance. Operator gas funding uses only the operator treasury’s tokens through a contract limited to fixed gas-wallet recipients. User inheritance assets are not used for operator gas. Each factory’s strategy, 10% service fee and recipient are immutable, with no admin upgrade or strategy-switch powers. Morpho strategies have separate curator and governance risks. No independent third-party security audit has been performed. Read the app’s Privacy Policy, Terms and Yield Terms.
